 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

At Gwalior
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice G. S. Ahluwalia
 On The 25th Of March, 2026
 Miscellaneous Second Appeal No. 30 of 2025
 Shri Shivam Sengar
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh
 Appearance:

Shri Deependra Singh Raghuwanshi, Advocate for the ap
 Shri Rajendra Jain, Govt. Advocate for respondent/Sta

Order 
This miscellaneous second appeal, under section 71(6) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short "the Act") has been filed against the judgment dated 2/4/2025 passed by the Food Safety Appellate Tribunal/ IX District Judge, Gwalior in RCA No. 289/2024, by which the appeal filed by the appellant has been dismissed and the order dated 13/9/2024 passed by the Adjudicating Authority/Additional District Magistrate, Gwalior in Case No. Q/Food Safety/66/2022, was affirmed.

sentences.text:
2. Facts necessary for disposal of the present appeal, in short, are that on 8/10/2021 at about 6:30 p.m., Collector, Gwalior received a complaint and accordingly on the instructions of Collector,
Gwalior, the Food Safety Officer along with his team, went to Platform No.1 of Railway Station,
Gwalior where Railway DSP and Tahsildar also met them.
It was found that Mava and Paneer were kept on Platform No.1.

When it was inquired from NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:10333 2 MSA-30-2025 the booking-counter, then it was informed by the Counter in-charge that Mava and Paneer have been booked by Shivam Sengar on his own ID as well as IDs of Pradeep Jain, Hariram Baghel and Manoj Yadav.

Accordingly, Tahsildar Kuldeep Dubey,
after taking the mobile number of Shivam Sengar from the counter in-charge, called on the mobile number and it was found that Shivam Sengar was already sitting on platform No.1.

When Shivam Shri Shivam Sengar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 25 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44403211/
1 Sengar was inquired about Mava and Paneer, then he informed that he has booked the goods for sending it to Bhopal.

sentences.text: Accordingly, with the consent of Shivam Sengar, the booking was cancelled and the goods were taken into custody.
Thereafter, information was given to Police Station, Padav and accordingly, the police force came and brought Shivam Sengar to police station Padav along with the seized articles.
Since the Food Safety Officer was under an apprehension that the Mava and Paneer may be of substandard quality, therefore, the samples were taken with the consent of Shivam Sengar.
The total value of the seized goods was Rs.3,76,000/-.
The seized articles were sent to the laboratory for report of Food Analyst.
As per the report of the Food Analyst, the Mava was found within norms whereas the Paneer was found to be substandard.

After receiving the report of the Food Analyst, the copy of report was sent to the applicant to enable him to file an appeal and seek retesting by referral laboratory as provided under section 46(4) of the Act as well as Rule 2.4.2(6) of the Food Safety and Standard Rules, 2011 but no appeal was filed.
After completing the investigation, the complaint was filed.

3. Show cause notice was issued by the Adjudicating Officer, but the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:10333 3 MSA-30-2025 applicant did not file any reply and accordingly by order dated 11/4/2023, the right to file reply was closed.

The complainant examined Brijesh Kumar Shiromani as PW1 and the Adjudicating Authority, after hearing the parties, held that the applicant is guilty of violation of sections 51 and 58 of the Act and accordingly imposed a penalty of Rs.1,50,000/- for violating section 51 and Rs.50,000/- for violating section 58 of the Act and in total a fine of Rs. two lacs was imposed.

4. Being aggrieved by the order passed by the Adjudicating authority, applicant preferred an appeal which was registered as RCA No. 289/2024 and the Appellate Tribunal, by judgment dated 2/4/2025, dismissed the appeal.

5. Challenging the judgment passed by the Appellate Tribunal, as well as, the order of the Adjudicating Authority, it is submitted by counsel for applicant that the Food Safety Officer was not competent to seize the goods as well as collect samples from Platform No.1 of Railway Station,
Gwalior because as per the notification issued in the Official Gazette of India dated 17/6/2021, Shri Om Prakash Sharma was appointed as Food Safety Officer for Western Railway.
6. Considered the submissions made by counsel for the applicant.
7. It is fairly conceded by counsel for applicant that Food Safety Officer is having jurisdiction for the area for which he has been appointed.
It was not disputed that the Railway Platform No.1 of Gwalior Railway Station falls within the territorial jurisdiction of the Food Safety Officer.

The only contention of counsel for applicant is that since Shri Om Prakash Sharma NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:10333 4 MSA-30-2025 was appointed as the Food Safety Officer for Western Railway, therefore, it has to be presumed that the jurisdiction of the Food Safety Officer was taken away.
In the considered opinion of this court, the said submission made by counsel for applicant cannot be accepted.

Unless and until the jurisdiction of the Food Safety Officer is specifically taken away from him, he will have territorial jurisdiction to seize and collect samples even from the area falling within the jurisdiction of Western Railway.

sentences.text:
Under these circumstances, it is held that in absence of any withdrawal of powers from the regular Food Safety Officer in respect of area falling within the jurisdiction of Western Railway,
merely because Shri Om Prakash Sharma was appointed as a Food Safety Officer for Western Railway, it cannot be said that the regular Food Safety Officer had no jurisdiction to inspect, seize and take the samples of the goods from the area belonging to the Western Railway.
9.

At this stage, it is submitted by counsel for applicant that it is clear from the complaint that Mava and Paneer were booked with the ID of three more persons but they were not prosecuted and under these circumstances, it is submitted that prosecution of the applicant, who was found present on the Railway Station at Platform No.1 and on whose ID also the goods were seized, is bad.
10. Considered the aforesaid submission made by counsel for applicant.
11. Merely because some of the other persons who might have committed an offence or who might have acted in violation of sections 51 NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:10333 5 MSA-30-2025 and 58 of the Act were not prosecuted, it would not mean that the person who was found in immediate possession of the Mava and Paneer and was also found on the Railway Platform No.1 of Gwalior Railway Station cannot be prosecuted.
The prosecution of the applicant cannot be set aside merely because other persons, who also might have violated the provisions of section 51 and 58 of the Act, were not prosecuted.
12. No other argument is advanced by counsel for the applicant.
13. Under these circumstances, this Court is of considered opinion that no case is made out warranting interference.

14. Accordingly, the judgment dated 2/4/2025 passed by the Food Safety Appellate Tribunal/ IX District Judge, Gwalior in RCA No. 289/2024, as well as, order dated 13/9/2024 passed by the Adjudicating Authority/Additional District Magistrate, Gwalior in Case No. Q/Food Safety/66/2022 are hereby affirmed.

entities.text: Food Safety Appellate Tribunal/ IX District Judge, Gwalior
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 15. The appeal fails and is, hereby, dismissed.

(G. S. AHLUWALIA) JUDGE (and)
